source:
Create a AAA-quality endless runner for Roblox inspired by the fast-paced gameplay of classic endless runners like Temple Run 2. The experience should capture the same adrenaline, fluid movement, exploration, and progression while using entirely original characters, environments, animations, music, sounds, UI, and level assets.
The game should feel polished enough to compete with top Roblox experiences.
Core Gameplay
Create an endless runner where the player automatically runs forward.
The player can:
 • Swipe Left → Turn Left
 • Swipe Right → Turn Right
 • Swipe Up → Jump
 • Swipe Down → Slide
 • Collect coins
 • Dodge obstacles
 • Navigate branching paths
 • Achieve high scores
 • Complete missions
 • Unlock cosmetics and characters
Movement should be smooth and highly responsive.

Motion Controls
On supported mobile devices, add optional motion controls using the device's accelerometer and gyroscope.
Features:
 • Tilt left/right to steer or subtly change lane position
 • Optional head-look camera effect
 • Motion sensitivity slider
 • Calibration screen
 • Toggle motion controls on/off
 • Automatic fallback to swipe controls if motion sensors are unavailable
 • Low-latency filtering to reduce jitter
 • Dead zones and smoothing for comfortable play
Motion controls should enhance gameplay without replacing core swipe controls.

Endless World Generation
Implement procedural generation that creates an endless path while maintaining handcrafted quality.
Include diverse original environments such as:
 • Ancient jungle ruins
 • Mountain temples
 • Lava caverns
 • Ice canyons
 • Desert ruins
 • Floating islands
 • Bamboo forests
 • Waterfalls
 • Forgotten cities
 • Underground caverns
Generation should avoid impossible obstacle combinations and maintain fair difficulty.

Obstacles
Create a large variety of original obstacles:
 • Gaps
 • Broken bridges
 • Fallen trees
 • Rolling boulders
 • Rotating blades
 • Swinging axes
 • Spike traps
 • Crumbling floors
 • Fire traps
 • Moving platforms
 • Collapsing bridges
 • Narrow ledges
 • Climbing sections
 • Rope swings
 • Zip lines
Difficulty should scale naturally as the run progresses.

Collectibles
Implement:
 • Coins
 • Rare gems
 • Power crystals
 • Treasure chests
 • Mystery relics
 • Keys
 • Daily collectibles
 • Seasonal collectibles

Power-ups
Create an extensible power-up system including:
 • Coin magnet
 • Temporary shield
 • Speed burst
 • Double coins
 • Slow-motion
 • Invincibility
 • Extra life
 • Auto-collect
 • Lucky treasure boost
Each should include:
 • Visual effects
 • Audio feedback
 • UI timers
 • Upgrade paths

Enemy Chase
Create an original pursuing creature that keeps pressure on the player.
Features:
 • Dynamic catch-up system
 • Difficulty scaling
 • Different chase phases
 • Escape mechanics
 • Cinematic introductions
 • Intelligent obstacle interaction

Missions
Implement hundreds of procedurally generated missions such as:
 • Collect coins
 • Travel distance
 • Jump count
 • Slide count
 • Near misses
 • Perfect turns
 • Consecutive runs
 • Power-up usage
 • Treasure collection

Progression
Create long-term progression:
 • Character unlocks
 • Outfit customization
 • Cosmetic trails
 • Pets
 • Skill upgrades
 • Permanent upgrades
 • Daily rewards
 • Weekly events
 • Achievements
 • Prestige system

Graphics
Create high-quality original visuals featuring:
 • Dynamic lighting
 • Volumetric fog
 • Weather
 • Water effects
 • Particle systems
 • Animated foliage
 • Day/night cycle
 • Cinematic camera
 • Smooth animations
 • Optimized performance across devices

Audio
Compose completely original music inspired by adventurous orchestral and tribal themes.
Include:
 • Ambient exploration music
 • Chase music
 • Menu music
 • Victory sounds
 • Coin collection
 • Power-ups
 • Environmental ambience
Do not use copyrighted music.

Roblox Features
Integrate:
 • DataStore
 • ProfileService
 • Leaderboards
 • Badges
 • Daily rewards
 • Cloud saves
 • Cross-device support
 • Mobile optimization
 • Console support
 • PC support

Performance
Optimize for:
 • 60+ FPS on modern devices
 • Graceful quality scaling
 • Streaming Enabled compatibility
 • Efficient procedural generation
 • Object pooling
 • Minimal memory usage

Code Architecture
Use clean, modular Luau code with separate systems for:
 • Runner Controller
 • Input Manager
 • Motion Control Manager
 • Procedural Generation
 • Obstacle Manager
 • Collectible Manager
 • Mission System
 • Progression System
 • Save Manager
 • UI Framework
 • Audio Manager
 • Camera Controller

QA & Polish
Do not stop after the first playable version.
Continue iterating by:
 • Automatically testing every gameplay mechanic
 • Verifying procedural generation never creates impossible paths
 • Stress-testing long runs
 • Testing all motion controls across supported devices
 • Optimizing performance
 • Eliminating bugs
 • Refining animations, controls, camera, and game feel
Repeat testing and refinement until the experience is polished, performant, and feels like a premium endless runner with original content suitable for Roblox.

image_prompt.text: Gaps, spike traps, fire traps and the pursuing creature itself - anything that ends the run on contact
Rolling boulders, rotating blades, swinging axes, collapsing bridges and moving platforms timed against the player's current speed
Volumetric fog and sharp temple turns at the end of the chunk queue, masking the next stretch of world spawning in
Modular ruin, temple, cavern and canyon segments whose exit pivot matches the next segment's origin pivot, so a long run never drifts
Broken bridges, fallen trees, gaps and narrow ledges to hurdle as the path scrolls past

layout_placement.text: Coin trails, gems, power crystals, chests and relics laid along the riskier lines
Coin magnet, shield, speed burst, slow-motion and invincibility pickups placed along the run
A cleanup volume a fixed distance behind the camera recycling cleared chunks

notes: P6: the path is chunk rules, not a fixed map; spacing must be derived from current speed rather than authored in fixed studs.
Branching paths and 90-degree turns are central to the request and no option expresses them - the chunk rules must support forks.
Ten named biomes have to be expressed as chunk sets; the scale band describes one chunk run, not the world, which is endless.
Motion controls, missions, progression, audio and performance targets are outside the layout job.

open_questions.ask: How long should one generated stretch be before the biome changes?
How often should the path fork, and do the forks rejoin or commit the player to a branch?

theme: Ancient adventure ruins - jungle temples, lava caverns, ice canyons, desert ruins

coverage_missing.ask: Are the turns 90-degree corners like Temple Run, or gentle curves?
Should biomes change on a distance schedule or at branch points?
How wide is the runnable corridor - three lanes' worth or wider?

answers.ask: How long should one generated stretch be before the biome changes?
answers.answer: Use short, readable biome stretches of roughly 60–90 seconds of running before transitioning to the next environment, with a brief blended transition segment.

answers.ask: How often should the path fork, and do the forks rejoin or commit the player to a branch?
answers.answer: Present a fork about every 20–30 seconds on average, and have branches rejoin after a short alternate segment so runs remain procedurally manageable and fair.
